family: MOD_3 zero-residue family defined in proof.md Section 1: L is the set of binary strings (including the empty string) whose number of ones is divisible by 3; for every integer n>=0, f_n(x)=1 iff x_1+...+x_n == 0 (mod 3). So f_0=1. One linear-time evaluator decides L at every length; the NP verifier accepts exactly an empty witness together with an input in L, witness bound 0.
theorem: For this one fixed total uniform family (in P, hence in NP with empty witnesses), C_B2(f_n)>=2n-6 for every integer n>=3 at actual input length n=|x| in the full Li–Yang B2 model; hence C_B2(f_n)>=2n-o(n) at every sufficiently large integer length, i.e. liminf C_B2(f_n)/n>=2.
